svg.text: Gated DeltaNet in one picture: a memory table that rewrites and forgets
18 of Qwen3.5's 24 layers; chapter 7 (the recurrence) and chapter 8 (chunked parallelism) of Transformer by Hand
① Why: don't store the whole context as it is
Full attention: every token looks back over all earlier K, V
KV cache: 4 KB more per token, and slower and slower to compute
Gated DeltaNet: squeeze the context into one fixed-size table
rewritten for every token, read by looking up with q
16 heads per layer, 1 MB in total (fp32), whatever the context
② The memory table = a key → value dictionary
Write: S ← S + k·vᵀ (outer product, added in)
Read: o = Sᵀ·q (mixed by q's similarity to each k)
Link to attention: drop softmax, Σ(q·kⱼ)·vⱼ = (Σ kⱼ·vⱼᵀ)ᵀ·q;
the bracket is this table, added to as the context arrives: hence "linear" attention
③ Step by step: the table has k₁→[3, 1], k₂→[−1, 2]; now k₁ should become [5, 0]
just add the new row on top:
DeltaNet: look up, write the difference
one gradient step on k, β is the learning rate
Gated DeltaNet: decay first, then write
the whole table × α first (0.5 here)
old memories not written again fade ✓
With α = 0.9: 35% of old content left after 10 steps, only 0.5% after 50
④ Four steps per token (chapter 7's delta_rule)
⑤ Qwen3.5's shell: each token computes its own α, β
q, k, v first glance at their previous 3 tokens
q and k normalized to unit length
keeps writes and lookups at a stable scale
same idea as chapter 6's gate: say less this time
this is all of a layer's "memory"
⑥ The table blurs, so every 3 linear layers get 1 full-attention layer
Put n (k, v) pairs into one 128 × 128 table, read each back with its k, and look at the error:
128-dim keys have at most 128 non-interfering directions; the delta rule favours recent writes, but only "roughly remembers"
L = Gated DeltaNet (18 layers): cheap, the gist
F = full attention (6 layers): precise look-back
e.g. quoting an earlier sentence word for word
⑦ Chunked parallelism (chapter 8): 64 tokens per chunk, all at once inside, one table between chunks
The catch: within a chunk, later tokens wait for earlier writes
uₜ = what token t really writes into the table
lower triangular: one solve_triangular gives every u
With U, everything else is matmuls:
table at the chunk's end S = S₀ + Kᵀ·U
with decay: each term × exp(Gᵢ − Gⱼ)
Too small a chunk starves the GPU,
too large becomes T × T; 64 is the compromise
T steps → T/64. One layer, 279 tokens: chunked ~10× faster, outputs within ~1e-7. Prefill and training chunk; decode uses the recurrence
2021 DeltaNet: linear attention writes with the delta rule (Schlag et al.)
2024 DeltaNet trained in parallel over chunks (Yang et al.)
2025 on Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 mix it 3:1; Kimi Linear's KDA is a variant
